Privacy.intro: Privacy Buy is retired. Recover an existing ETH deposit using your recovery file and original depositing wallet. No deposit approval is needed.

preview: Deposit 50,000 $CLAUS to mint one of 300 NFTs. Each NFT holds those tokens and can be burned to redeem them.
Holders share ETH trading fees through automatic daily payouts. Open NFT Vaults to mint, view your NFTs or redeem their tokens.
NFTs.intro: 300 different Clauses, each with 50,000 $CLAUS inside. I took inspiration from Unipeg and built the NFT mechanism into my Uniswap v4 hook.
body: Deposit 50,000 $CLAUS to mint an available NFT. Each wallet can mint once, with its character drawn at random. You can also buy or receive more NFTs. The tokens stay inside each NFT until its owner burns it to redeem them. Selling the NFT passes that backing to the buyer.

While you hold an NFT, you earn a share of the pool’s fees. The hook sets aside 0.35% of eligible ETH trading volume from the existing project fee. The earlier reward boost no longer affects fees. Every character has the same earning weight; your share reflects how many you held and for how long during each daily period.
After each period closes, ETH rewards are sent to eligible wallets automatically. You don’t need to claim them. Amounts depend on trading activity and holding time, so they change from day to day.

body.text: The first 24-hour reward period earned holders roughly $11,000. Those ETH payments are complete. The Journal records the payout and links to its onchain evidence.

body: I want these NFTs to open up more features and privileges across the Claus ecosystem. I’ll share the specifics as those take shape.

Arena.intro: Rising Tide is retired. New game sessions are closed and historical scores are preserved.

Arbitrage.title: Pool Arbitrage
Arbitrage.intro: I’ve removed the arbitrage function from my pool hook. Its trading worker and the separate buybacks funded by arbitrage profit are stopped.
body: The earlier version bought $CLAUS where it was cheaper and sold it where it was dearer, in one transaction. After execution costs and reserves, available profit could fund separate buybacks for the project wallet.
The token address, pool and other functions remain in place. NFT rewards, ordinary burns and participating LP rewards continue.
Any future arbitrage integration will be a separate change with its own review and Journal entry. The removal entry records what changed and links to the transaction.

preview: Each main-pool trade contributes a total 2.30% fee.
See the live allocation and the project wallet.
Funding.intro: Trading fees fund the project, NFT holders, burns and participating liquidity providers.
body: The fixed split is 1.30% owner, 0.35% NFT rewards, 0.15% buyback and burn, 0.20% LP rewards and 0.30% Programmable, measured on gross ETH trade value.
While no qualifying position is staked, the 0.20% goes to the owner, making the owner share 1.50%. It is not saved for later entrants. With zero NFT supply, its 0.35% also goes to the owner.
Weather no longer changes fees. Old reserves and earned rewards keep their original purpose.

preview: A fixed 0.15% of main-pool trade value funds CLAUS buybacks and burns.
The supply tracker includes direct holder burns.
Burn.intro: Trading fees buy CLAUS from the pool and burn the purchased tokens.
body: The fixed 0.15% allocation is part of the existing 2.30% total fee. Weather no longer changes it.
The supply tracker measures all tokens burned since launch.

Liquidity.title: LP Rewards
preview: Provide both ETH and CLAUS to the main pool. Voluntarily stake a qualifying full-range position to earn daily ETH rewards.
While nobody is staked, its 0.20% fee allocation goes to the owner.
Liquidity.intro: Participating liquidity providers share native ETH rewards, weighted by liquidity multiplied by time.
body: The 0.20% allocation applies only while qualifying liquidity is staked. Empty-period fees go to the owner, never retroactively to later entrants.
Rewards use the NFT reward clock with a separate ledger. Existing NFT backing, redemption and 0.35% rewards are unchanged.
Unstake to recover the original position NFT, then remove liquidity through PositionManager. Earned rewards survive unstaking and failed delivery. Asset amounts and value may change.
Future automatic LP funding is retired. Previously collected reserves remain with the original position and reconciliation history.

Weather.title: Weather Switch (retired)
Weather.intro: Weather no longer changes the main-pool fee allocation.
body: The burn allocation is fixed at 0.15%. Participating staked LPs share 0.20%; while nobody is staked that share goes to the owner.
Historical observations and paid provider records remain retained.

preview: FOMO buybacks have been retired. New trades no longer allocate fees to this function.
Previously collected funds keep their original purpose. This page records completed deliveries.
Buybacks.intro: FOMO buybacks have been retired. Their former 0.15% now goes to project revenue, bringing that share to 1.15%.
body: The total main-pool fee remains 2.3%. NFT rewards remain 0.35%; burns and participating LP rewards use their current fixed allocations.
Funds collected before retirement remain reserved for delivery to the existing FOMO wallet. They are not reassigned to project revenue.
The counters show historical completed deliveries and ETH spent. They do not show the wallet’s current balance or promise that a pending batch has executed.

preview: The token’s name and ticker can change while its contract address, balances and pool stay the same. Holders keep the same tokens.
Open Token Identity to check the current name and contract. Changes are recorded in the Journal; wallets and trading sites may update their labels later.
Name.intro: Claus can change the token’s name and ticker after launch. The contract address stays the same, so holders do not need to move their tokens.
body: A metadata update changes the name and ticker displayed by the token contract. It leaves balances, the contract address and the pool in place. The Journal keeps a record of each change, including earlier names.
The token is named Claus and uses the ticker CLAUS. A different token can copy those words, so the contract address is the reference for identifying the official token.
Trading sites and wallets may cache an earlier name after an update. Check the contract and Journal if their labels differ.
